title: fix(objectql): a refused sys_file read marks the file field refused instead of reading as no file
body:
Fixes #22593
Clause-②: yes

## What changes

A file field (`file` / `image` / `avatar` / `video` / `audio`) holds a `sys_file` id. The engine expands that id by reading `sys_file` as the caller (`ObjectQL.resolveFileReferences`, `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`). A reader who may read the record but not `sys_file` gets that sub-read refused. The record still came back, but with the bare id in the field. A bare id is also what an uncommitted id or a storage outage leaves behind, so the console showed "no file" and the server logged a `warn` telling the operator to check storage.

After this change, the security layer's refusal (`PERMISSION_DENIED`) marks each held id as refused, in the value itself:

- **From:** `{ "attachment": "f_7cQx2Lm90a" }`, plus `warn: sys_file lookup failed; file fields keep their raw ids and will render as "no file" for this read`.
- **To:** `{ "attachment": { "id": "f_7cQx2Lm90a", "metadataRefused": true } }`. Multi-value fields mark each id, and a legacy URL string in the array passes through unchanged. The refusal is logged at `debug` only, because the reader is told in the value (AGENTS "Degradation log levels": a failure handed to the caller).
- **Unchanged:**
  - A reader with `sys_file` read still gets the hydrated `{ id, name, size, mimeType, url }`.
  - An empty field still reads empty.
  - A missing `sys_file` table still leaves the bare id, silently.
  - Any other failure (connection, timeout, a database-level ACL fault such as `42501`) still leaves the bare id with the existing `warn`.
  - The record read still succeeds. Fail-open is unchanged.

Nothing that was not read is served: the marker has no `name`, `size`, `mimeType` or `url`. A consumer that needs a link builds the stable `/api/v1/storage/files/:fileId` endpoint from the id, as it already does for a bare id. The download door makes its own access decision (see "Not in this PR").

`@objectstack/spec` declares the shape. `FileRefusedValueSchema` / `FileRefusedValue` is a closed `{ id, metadataRefused: true }`, an ADR-0122 isomorphic alias pinned in `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` (773 to 774). `valueSchemaFor(def, 'expanded')` for the file types now accepts it beside the bare id and `FileValueSchema`. It is a read form only: the stored form stays the bare id, and a pin checks that `valueSchemaFor(def)` (the stored form) rejects the marker object. Changeset: `@objectstack/objectql` minor and `@objectstack/spec` minor, with the FROM and TO above.

## Measured on main first (the symptom, before the change)

Both pin files were run against `main`'s `engine.ts` (`d748ae80af`, blob `df2300664b`, byte-identical by `git hash-object`), with every other file at this head (`faf689872c`). The file was then restored from `HEAD` (blob `1d1b78f500`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty).

- Real security layer (`plugin-security/src/file-field-hydration-refused.test.ts`, real `ObjectQL` + `SecurityPlugin` + `SqlDriver`): the reader with record read and no `sys_file` read got `attachment === 'f_7cQx2Lm90a'`, the bare id. 1 failed and 3 passed. The 3 that passed are the two controls and the direct-refusal probe, which shows `sys_file` refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403.
- Seam pins (`objectql/src/engine-file-hydrate-refused.test.ts`): 4 failed and 4 passed. The `warn` captured on main is exactly the line from the report: `sys_file lookup failed; file fields keep their raw ids and will render as "no file" for this read`. The 4 controls passed on main as well.

The symptom from the 17.7.0 report reproduces on current `main`.

## Pins (green at `faf689872c`)

- A reader without `sys_file` read sees `{ id, metadataRefused: true }`, through both `find` and `findOne`, on the real security layer and on the seam.
- Control: a record with no file still reads `null`.
- Control: a reader with `sys_file` read gets the hydrated file.
- Control: a missing `sys_file` table (`42P01`) still reads the bare id, with no `warn`.
- Control: a database-level ACL fault (`42501`) is an outage, not a refusal of this caller. It still reads the bare id and still logs the seam's `warn`.
- The served value parses as `FileRefusedValueSchema` and as `valueSchemaFor(def, 'expanded')`, and carries exactly the keys `id` and `metadataRefused`.

## Ablation

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the anchor `if (isReadRefusal(error)) {` with `if (false && isReadRefusal(error)) {`, which restores the fall-through.

- The anchor hit once (count 1 to 0), and the blob changed from `1d1b78f500` to `1565ec17ca`.
- objectql pins: 4 failed and 4 passed. The first pin received the bare id.
- plugin-security pins: 1 failed and 3 passed. The first pin received the bare id.
- Restore: the blob equals `HEAD` (`1d1b78f500`), `git diff HEAD` is empty and the porcelain status is clean.

Both legs read source, not `dist/`: the objectql test imports `./engine`, and plugin-security's `vitest.config.ts` aliases `@objectstack/objectql` to `../../objectql/src/index.ts`.

## Cross-lane paths (the seat declares these on the lane posts before this PR leaves draft)

- `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts`, its pins (`field-value.test.ts`, `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`, and `scripts/strictness-ledger.test.ts`, whose site count over `field-value.zod.ts` moves from 3 to 4) and the regenerated spec artifacts (`api-surface/`, `authorable-surface/`, `declaration-map/`, `export-origins/`, `json-schema.manifest/` data shards) are `domain:spec`.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/file-field-hydration-refused.test.ts` (test only) is `domain:services`.
- `content/docs/references/data/field-value.mdx` and `content/docs/references/index.mdx` (generated by spec `build-docs`) are `domain:devx`.
- `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/data.md` (generated, `check:strictness-ledger`) gets +1 strict site in `data/`. `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.md` gets a one-row update on the `field-value.zod.ts` row naming the third `strictObject`.

## Consumer relay (objectui, not edited here)

At objectui `origin/main` `12ff256`, `packages/fields/src/widgets/file-value.ts` `readFileValue` takes the marker through its object arm:

- The id is kept, and the URL is built from the id (`fileUrlFromId`).
- The name falls back to the generic "File", and there is no `mimeType`.
- `metadataRefused` is not carried onto `FileValueView`.

So today the console already shows a non-empty generic file chip, not `EmptyValue`, but the refusal itself never reaches the UI. What the console's file renderers (`FileField` read-only list, `FileCell`, `ImageField`, `AvatarField`, the grid cell) should show for `metadataRefused: true`:

- A distinct restricted state: a lock affordance and a translated label (for example "File (details restricted)"), not the generic fallback name.
- Never `EmptyValue`.
- No thumbnail attempt for image or avatar types, because no MIME type is known.
- Keep the open/download affordance on the id-derived stable endpoint. That door decides on its own and may answer `403 FILE_DOWNLOAD_DENIED`.
- The editable widget submits only the bare id (`fileIdOf` already reads `id`), never the marker object.

Once objectui takes a spec that carries `FileRefusedValueSchema`, it can tell the form apart by shape.

## Not in this PR

- **The access half.** This PR makes no change to `sys_file`'s read rule. Whether file metadata should follow the read access of the parent record goes to the maintainer on a separate decision card, which the seat files. The inputs were measured read-only and are in the report on the card.
- Row-level narrowing on `sys_file` (a reader with object read whose sub-read comes back short) still reads as a bare id. The engine cannot tell a hidden row from an uncommitted one without an existence probe, and an existence probe is itself an access decision. It belongs to the access half.

## Acceptance notes

- Export: `formatCsvCell` already serialises an object-valued cell as JSON, so a refused reader's CSV cell now reads `{"id":"…","metadataRefused":true}` instead of the bare id. This is distinct from both empty and hydrated. XLSX and JSON export pass the value through.
- `plugin-approvals` `normalizeActionAttachment` would drop the marker (it maps any object to `{ id, name?, url? }`), but its only caller, `listActions`, reads `sys_approval_action` with the system context, so its hydration never sees a refusal.
- The header of `packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts` still says the default member permission sets grant wildcard CRUD. `member_default` has named no `'*'` since that wildcard was removed, so the comment is stale. This is noted only, not filed (carrier: none).

## Verification (head `faf689872c`, which is `origin/main` `d748ae80af` merged in)

- Build: `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-security...' build`, which covers spec, objectql and plugin-security in one closure. Then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` reported all 15 artifacts up to date.
- Full suites:
  - `@objectstack/objectql` `test`: 393 files and 7738 tests passed.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-security` `test`: 194 files, with 4079 passed and 45 skipped.
  - `@objectstack/spec` `test`: 640 files, with 19103 passed and 1 todo.
- `typecheck` passed for spec, objectql and plugin-security.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` derived 119 commands, and all 119 exited 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reads: 119 derived, 119 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, all with recorded exit codes.
- Narrowed lint over the 6 changed TypeScript files, with `eslint --no-inline-config --format json`:
  - The `--format json` output reports 6 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
  - The population comes from the `eslint.config.mjs` blocks for `packages/**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}`.
  - The config never enables type-aware linting, so this diff cannot change the verdict on any file it does not touch.
  - The repository-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- Not run locally, left to CI: the 6 path-scheduled CI jobs and the workspace type-check lanes that the derivation lists as out of reach locally.
